title: ALMASOP. The Localized and Chemically Rich Features near the Bases of the Protostellar Jet in HOPS 87
question: What is the physical origin and chemical composition of the localized, chemically rich regions near the bases of the bipolar molecular outflow in the Class 0 protostellar core HOPS 87?

data.sensitivity: 2018.1.00302.S: ~12 uJy beam^-1 (continuum, also stated as 0.9 mJy beam^-1 in Fig 1) and ~3.3 mJy beam^-1 per channel; 2015.1.00341.S: ~6 mJy beam^-1 per 0.244 MHz channel

what.value: Bolometric luminosity L_bol = 38 +/- 13 L_sun, bolometric temperature T_bol = 36.7 +/- 14.5 K, and v_LSR = 11.4 km s^-1 for HOPS 87

evidence.quote: with a bolometric luminosity L bol of 38 ± 13 L ⊙, a bolometric temperature T bol of 36 . 7 ± 14 . 5 K, and local standard of rest velocity v LSR of 11 . 4 km s − 1 (Dutta et al. 2020).

what.value: Spectroscopic line parameters from CDMS and JPL databases

evidence.quote: Species E u f rest Quantum Number Database

recipe.goal: Evaluate 1.3 mm dust continuum optical depth and H2 column density at the continuum peak
recipe.method: Measure peak continuum brightness temperature and apply Planck function radiative transfer and column density equations from Kauffmann et al. (2008)
assumptions: Mean molecular weight per hydrogen molecule mu ~ 2.8
Dust opacity law kappa_nu = 0.1(nu/THz)^beta cm^2 g^-1 with beta = 1.70, giving kappa_nu = 0.0083 cm^2 g^-1 at 1.3 mm

recipe.goal: Create integrated intensity (moment-0) maps and channel maps of molecular transitions
recipe.method: Integrate emission over specified velocity ranges for each molecular transition to map spatial distributions of outflows, hot corino, and two-lobe features, and inspect high-resolution Cycle 3 channel maps
key_parameters: Velocity integration ranges: +/- 40 km s^-1 (CO, SiO), +/- 3 km s^-1 (13CS), +/- 7.5 km s^-1 (others)

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and Position-Velocity (PV) diagrams to analyze kinematics and line ratios
recipe.method: Extract continuum-subtracted spectra along the cavity/outflow axis (PA = -4 deg), generate PV diagrams along and across the outflow axis using CARTA 4.0, measure maximum velocity widths above 5 sigma, and compute flux density ratio PV diagrams
key_parameters: Outflow axis PA = -4 deg, centered at 1.3 mm continuum peak
Detection threshold = 5 sigma for velocity width and PV ratio calculations

evidence.quote: The brightness temperature of the 1.3 mm continuum peak is 47 K with a beam size of 0 ′′ . 42.
Adopting the brightness temperature at the continuum peak, the derived optical depth τ ν is 1.55, indicating that the continuum is somewhat optically thick.
Assuming a gas-to-dust ratio of 100, the resulting molecular hydrogen column density N (H 2 ) is 2 . 89 × 10 25 cm − 2 .

score_reason: Both ALMA datasets are public (with ARI-L products directly usable for Cycle 3), and the kinematic analysis in CARTA and continuum calculations are straightforward and clearly parameterized, though full re-imaging of Cycle 6 requires consulting Dutta et al. (2020).
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA datasets, straightforward morphological and PV-diagram analysis, and clear quantitative metrics (continuum optical depth, column density, lobe offsets, and velocity widths).
